Laser beam radius, characteristic length scale of the laser spot

variables.reason: The ledger variable 'rho' is explicitly defined in the problem as material density (mass per unit volume). The KB record pq_mass_density defines mass density as 'Mass per unit volume' for continuum/material contexts, which is exactly how density is used in laser-melt problems. This record therefore directly supports all nonzero coordinates (M=1, L=-3) of the proposed SI vector and excludes the alternative electrical-resistivity meaning by context (thermal/material problem).

The ledger variable 'Tl-T0' is given as the temperature difference between melting and ambient. KB record pq_temperature_difference defines 'Difference between two thermodynamic temperatures' and is used in heat-transfer contexts like laser melting. This record directly justifies Theta=1 and all other coordinates 0 for this variable.

The ledger variable 'r0' is defined as the laser beam radius (characteristic length of the laser spot). KB record pq_laser_beam_radius explicitly defines that geometric length in the laser-material interaction domain, supporting L=1 and all other coordinates zero in the SI vector.

The problem lists 'alpha' as thermal diffusivity. KB record pq_thermal_diffusivity defines thermal diffusivity as k/(rho cp) with SI dimension L^2 T^-1 and notes its use in heat-transfer contexts. The laser-melt problem context (heat diffusion) selects this meaning over the alternative thermal-expansion meaning, so the record directly supports the given vector.

The ledger variable 'etaP' is stated as effective laser power (energy per unit time after absorptivity). KB record pq_effective_laser_power defines absorbed/effective laser power, notes that absorptivity is dimensionless, and gives SI dimensions of power (M L^2 T^-3). This aligns with the problem usage and supports the proposed vector.

The ledger variable 'cp' is given as heat capacity (per unit mass). KB record pq_specific_heat_capacity defines specific heat capacity (J kg^-1 K^-1) used in heat-transfer and thermodynamics contexts; its SI vector L^2 T^-2 Theta^-1 (with sign convention shown) corresponds exactly to the candidate exponents (Theta exponent negative in notation here indicates Theta^-1). The record therefore supports all coordinates of the proposed vector.

The ledger variable 'Vs' is the laser scan speed (beam velocity relative to material). KB record pq_scan_speed defines scan speed/translation velocity in laser-material interaction and gives SI dimension L T^-1, matching the candidate vector. The record directly applies to the variable as specified in the original problem.
